title: ALP Toolchain Pins v1
description: Validates metadata/toolchains.json -- the single source of truth for the pinned Zephyr SDK (cross-toolchain) release: its version, the per-artifact upstream URL + sha256 + size, and measured (not estimated) footprint numbers. A DECLARED, hand-maintained input (like metadata/bootstrap.json), never a step-execution DSL and never the resolved-identity concept metadata/schemas/alp-lock-v1.schema.json's reserved `toolchain` key is for. scripts/check_toolchain_lock.py is the drift gate that keeps this file, metadata/bootstrap.json's zephyr.version, and each CI workflow's own SDK reference in lockstep -- see that script's own module docstring for the full list of checks it runs; do not restate that list here, it will only drift again.

_comment.description: The file's own contract statement: a declared pin, not a resolved-identity record, and not a step-execution DSL. Kept as a real JSON field (not a comment) since JSON has no native comment syntax.

schemaVersion.description: This manifest's own contract version, independent of bootstrap.json's schemaVersion or alp-lock's lockVersion.

version.description: The pinned Zephyr SDK (sdk-ng) release, e.g. '1.0.1'. MUST equal the `SDK_VERSION` file at the Zephyr revision metadata/bootstrap.json's `zephyr.version` pins -- check_toolchain_lock.py enforces this by reading the pinned Zephyr checkout, not by trusting this field alone.

versionDerivation.description: Human-readable statement of where `version` comes from (Zephyr's own SDK_VERSION file at the pinned revision) -- the fact that makes a stale/invented value checkable rather than a silent copy-paste.

baseUrl.description: Canonical upstream release directory for `version` -- every artifact's URL is this base plus its own `filename`. Never a rehosted/mirrored URL (see docs/adr/0021-toolchain-provisioning.md's Decision on why alp-sdk pins origin instead).

artifacts.description: One row per (host, component) pair this SDK release ships. Not required to be exhaustive -- only rows an actual alp-sdk path reads need to be listed (see this file's own top-level `_comment` on the omitted linux-aarch64 row).

measuredFootprint.description: Measured (not estimated) install-size facts, replacing docs/adr/0021-toolchain-provisioning.md's unmeasured ~1 GB / ~17 GB figures. Deliberately does not resolve the hosttools/--no-hosttools trade-off it documents -- see `notes`.

notes.description: Human-readable lines, safe to print or quote verbatim -- an ARRAY (the same convention metadata/bootstrap.json's nativeLibHints.*.note already uses) so a long measurement writeup doesn't collapse into one unwrapped paragraph.

compressedDownloadBytes.description: Measured compressed download size in bytes, keyed by a human-readable label naming exactly which artifacts were summed (e.g. 'linux-x86_64-minimal-plus-arm-zephyr-eabi').

wholeSdk.description: Total on-disk bytes for the measured install (du -sb of the whole SDK root).

hosttools.description: On-disk bytes under hosttools/ alone -- the optional host-tool bundle (carries dtc) `west sdk install` installs by default.

gnuArmZephyrEabi.description: On-disk bytes under gnu/arm-zephyr-eabi/ alone -- the cross-compiler itself.

host.description: The host triple this artifact runs ON (not the target it cross-compiles for, which is always the embedded Cortex-M side). linux-aarch64 is a permitted value with no row required -- see this file's top-level `_comment`.

component.description: 'minimal-sdk' is the base zephyr-sdk-<version>_<host>_minimal archive (setup.sh + host tools, no cross-compilers); 'arm-zephyr-eabi-toolchain' is the individual arm-zephyr-eabi cross-toolchain archive setup.sh installs into it.

filename.description: Exact upstream release-asset filename, appended to zephyrSdk.baseUrl to form the download URL.

sizeBytes.description: Exact asset size in bytes, from the GitHub releases API `size` field -- a verified fact, not an estimate.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex sha256 of the exact asset, from upstream's own published sha256.sum for this release -- copied verbatim, never computed or retyped by hand.

tier.description: ADR 0021 SS3's consent-screen tier (issue #1603, follow-on to #1574's metadata/bootstrap.json `artifactProvenance.*.tier`, same enum). A -- hermetic or signed-package-manager delivered, no elevation: install after one consent click. B -- needs elevation (drivers, udev rules, WSL2 enablement): prompt once, stay skippable. C -- licence-gated third party: never silently fetched, show the licence, then verify. Every row in this file is 'A' today -- the ADR 0021 SS3 table places the Zephyr SDK and arm-zephyr-eabi there explicitly -- because both components ship as sha256-verified hermetic archives fetched with no elevation; the enum stays open so a future artifact in this file (there is none today) is not forced into the wrong tier.

licence.description: SPDX licence identifier for the artifact's primary licence, or null. null means the upstream project is genuinely multi-component (more than one licence covers different files/submodules of the same distributed archive) and cannot be honestly reduced to a single SPDX id without a file-level audit this repo has not performed -- an absent value, not a guessed one, per issue #1574's precedent (its own `xz`/`7zip` entries) and issue #1603's explicit instruction that a fabricated licence string on a consent screen is worse than an absent one. Both components in this file are null today: sdk-ng's own repository licence (Apache-2.0) covers its build scripts, not what the archives themselves contain -- `minimal-sdk` bundles openocd/qemu/bossa/gperf/dtc and `arm-zephyr-eabi-toolchain` bundles binutils-gdb/gcc/picolibc as separate upstream projects under their own licences (verified against sdk-ng's `.gitmodules` at the pinned v1.0.1 tag; see metadata/toolchains.json's `measuredFootprint.notes` for the full citation). A non-null value would be a real, verifiable fact about the named upstream project.
